'''''Pachyphytum bracteosum''''', the '''large-bracted pachyphytum''', is a perennial [[succulent]] native to [[Mexico]], occurring on rocks at altitudes between {{convert|1200-1800|m|abbr=on}}. The succulent has a [[diploid number]] of 66 or 132. The closest relatives of the plant are ''[[Pachyphytum oviferum]]'' and ''[[Pachyphytum longifolium]]''.<ref>{{cite book |page= 191 |title= Illustrated Handbook of Succulent Plants: Crassulaceae |volume= 6 |editor= Urs Eggli |edition= illustrated, reprint |publisher= Springer Science & Business Media |year= 2003 |isbn= 9783540419655}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Pachyphytum bracteosum.JPG|thumb|The plant flowering]]
''Pachyphytum bracteosum'' is a leafy and fleshy succulent. The leafy stems grow up to {{convert|30|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|25-38|mm|abbr=on}} thick. Fallen leaves form circular [[leaf scar]]s low on the stem. The purplish or bluish green leaves are thick and flattened. The leaves are [[oblanceolate]] and [[terete]], growing upwards of {{convert|5|cm|abbr=on}} long. Lower leaves grow at a right angle to the stem; upper leaves are erect or curved. The [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]s grow upwards of {{convert|30|cm|abbr=on}} long. The simple and elongate flowering stem grows {{convert|20-61|cm|abbr=on}} long. The flowering stem is curved at the apex and is [[secund]]. The numerous [[bract]]s are arranged in two [[wikt:imbrication|imbricated]] rows and have short [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]s. The five [[sepal]]s are unequal, with two long obtuse, lateral sepals and three other shorter sepals. The lateral sepals are oblong and approximately {{convert|8.4|mm|abbr=on}} long. The dark red [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]] has five spreading lobes and is about {{convert|5.1|mm|abbr=on}} long. The five [[stamen]]s that alternate with the petals are free from the corolla, while the other five are borne on the petals. The five erect [[carpel]]s each have a broad scale at their base.<ref>{{cite book |page= 53 |title= Addisonia: Colored Illustrations and Popular Descriptions of Plants, Part 3 |volume= 2 |publisher= New York Botanical Garden |year= 1917}}</ref> The [[anther]]s are ovate, the [[Style (botany)|style]]s are [[wikt:subulate|subulate]], and the [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]]s are [[wikt:capitate|capitate]].<ref name=Curtis>{{cite book |page= 4951 |title= Curtis's Botanical Magazine |volume= 82 |author= Sir William Jackson Hooker |author2= David Prain |author3= Otto Stapf |publisher= Reeve Brothers |year= 1856}}</ref>

The plant flowers in the summer.<ref name=Curtis/>
